newsitem.title: USA: U.S. credit union regulator backs new member rule.
newsitem.headline: U.S. credit union regulator backs new member rule.

text.p: The nation's credit union regulators on Thursday adopted a new rule aimed at limiting the impact of a recent court decision affecting membership policies for the lower-cost credit organizations.

At a meeting here, the National Credit Union Administration adopted a policy that allows employees of different companies to belong to the same credit union as long as the companies are in related fields.
The board also authorized a "group community" charter, allowing a credit union to serve specific occupational, associational and community groups within a well defined area.
The agency issued the rule, which is effective immediately on an interim basis, in response to a U.S. District Court ruling last month that affects 3,500 credit unions nationwide.
"What we are doing today will substantially and significantly alleviate some of the pain," NCUA Chairman Norman D'Amours said. "We don't consider this fixed."
D'Amours said the agency would continue to pursue legal and legislative remedies in the wake of the court decision.
In the ruling the judge said the credit union administration was not permitted to allow occupational federal credit unions to admit members who did not share a common bond of occupation.
It remains unclear whether credit unions will be forced to expel current members who work for companies in unrelated fields.
NCUA attorneys maintain that their new membership policy is consistent with the recent court ruling.
